frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Four spectral windows of 2 GHz each, 15.6 MHz frequency resolution

evidence.quote: Four spectral windows each covered a bandwidth of $2$ GHz (${\sim}750$ km s$^{-1}$ at the frequency of CO $J=6-5$), with a frequency resolution of $15.6$ MHz.
The CO $J = 6-5$ data set was obtained from the ALMA archive
with a total of 37 antennas in the $12$ m array
with baselines between $17.5$ and $555.5$ m
The resulting beam size is $0.23\ensuremath{''}\,\times\,0.21\ensuremath{''}$ (PA ${\sim}15\ensuremath{^\circ}$).
the final sensitivity achieved was $15$ mJy beam$^{-1}$ per $20$ km s$^{-1}$ (${\sim}46$ MHz) channel
The total on-source time for the observations was $272$ s
The data were taken on 2015 May 19
obtained from the ALMA archive (project 2013.1.00524.S, PI N. Lu)

findings_qualitative.value: CO 6-5 wing emission is oriented roughly perpendicular to the overall rotation, supporting an outflow.

evidence.loc: 3.3 CO J=6-5 line and 690 GHz continuum emission
evidence.quote: The wing emission is oriented along an axis that is approximately perpendicular to the overall rotation of the CO $J=6-5$ and $J=2-1$ emission.

claims.hypothesis: Do the CO line wings trace a nuclear molecular outflow?
claims.experiment: Compare SMA CO 2-1, ALMA CO 6-5 and VLA OH absorption line profiles and morphology
claims.result: CO wings to ±300 km/s; ALMA wings spatially separated perpendicular to rotation; OH blue wings to -300 km/s
claims.finding: Wings are signatures of a nuclear molecular outflow

evidence.quote: ALMA observations of CO $J=6-5$ at $0.2\ensuremath{''}$ resolution reveal similar line wings which are spatially separated along an axis approximately perpendicular to the overall velocity field of the galaxy.

claims.hypothesis: Is the outflow related to the minor-axis radio feature?
claims.experiment: Compare CO 6-5 wing PA with radio feature PA

evidence.loc: 4.4 Is the outflowing molecular gas entrained by a radio jet?
evidence.quote: the nuclear CO $J=6-5$ outflow (PA ${\sim}105\ensuremath{^\circ}$) does not have the same position angle as the radio feature (PA ${\sim}130\ensuremath{^\circ}$)

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Wings could be rapidly rotating gas rather than an outflow; outflow favoured due to OH blue wings at similar velocity.

evidence.quote: Although this could also be interpreted as a signature of rapidly rotating gas in the center of the the nucleus

limitations_admitted.value: Large resolution difference between CO 6-5 and 2-1 precludes detailed excitation analysis.

evidence.quote: the large difference in angular resolution between the CO $J=6-5$ and $J=2-1$ observations complicates the matter, precluding a detailed analysis

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA flux calibration uncertain by factor 2 and only 272 s on source
Blue wing reaches the band edge, so wing extent is a lower limit
Outflow interpretation is qualitative; no mass or rate estimated

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA data obtained from the archive

missing_for_reproduction: Wing velocity integration limits relative to defined systemic velocity
reproducibility.score_reason: Public data and robust given, but ALMA processing is thinly described and results are mostly qualitative.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: ALMA recipe is incomplete and results largely qualitative.
